title: In situ PCR using leaf epidermal peels
author: Diep R R Ganguly
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.p85dry6
materials: Once stain has developed, pipette off BM purple.

steps.title: Prepare sealed slides
steps.instruction: Place frame seals on a glass slide, press the borders to seal, heat the sealed slides in a thermal cycler at 90 °C for 10 min, then cut off excess seal so the slide fits properly in the PCR machine.

steps.title: Make fresh fixative
steps.instruction: Prepare on ice a fixative containing 63 % ethanol, 5 % acetic acid, and 2 % formaldehyde; keep it on ice and use within 3 hours.

steps.title: Wash slides with Buffer 1
steps.instruction: Wash each slide three times for 10 min with 100 µl of ice‑cold Wash Buffer 1 (63 % ethanol, 5 % glacial acetic acid) at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare enzyme mastermixes
steps.instruction: Set up the Turbo DNase (Ambion) mastermix and the reverse‑transcription (RT) mix using either Thermoscript RT or SuperScript III according to the manufacturers’ instructions.

steps.title: Bring plants to fume hood
steps.instruction: Transfer plants, fixative, microscope slides and frame‑seals to a fume hood; keep all items on ice for the upcoming fixation and washes.

steps.title: Add fixative to slides
steps.instruction: Pipette 100 µl of the prepared fixative onto each microscope slide.

steps.title: Make epidermal peels
steps.instruction: Using a fine paintbrush, peel 3–5 moderate‑sized leaf epidermal sections per slide and place them directly into the fixative on the slide; randomise peels across slides. Wear gloves and handle formaldehyde with care.

steps.title: Fix peels
steps.instruction: Incubate the peels in fixative for 45 min, refreshing the fixative with a pipette approximately every 15 min by evenly redistributing it across the peels.

steps.title: Remove excess fixative
steps.instruction: Wipe off any remaining liquid from the slides to ensure no formaldehyde remains. This is a safe pause point; proceed at the bench.

steps.title: Wash with PBS
steps.instruction: Wash the slides three times for 5 min each in 1× PBS (0.1 M Na₂HPO₄, 1.3 M NaCl, pH 7.5) stored at room temperature and less than one year old; after the final wash, remove as much buffer as possible.

steps.title: Heat‑inactivate
steps.instruction: Place the slides in a thermal cycler at 70 °C for 15 min, then immediately transfer them to ice (do not cool in the cycler to avoid glass cracking).

steps.title: Add EDTA
steps.instruction: Add 3 µl of 0.5 M EDTA to each slide to achieve a final concentration of 15 mM.

steps.title: Add DNase mastermix
steps.instruction: Remove the PBS solution and add 100 µl of the Turbo DNase mastermix to each slide.

steps.title: DNase incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the slides at 37 °C for 45 min.

steps.title: Allocate gene targets and controls
steps.instruction: Decide which genes will be analysed on each slide; include one positive house‑keeping control (e.g., 18S rRNA) and one no‑RT house‑keeping negative control.

steps.title: Wash after DNase
steps.instruction: Remove the DNase mix and wash the slides twice with ice‑cold sterilised water; keep the final wash on the slides until the RT mix is ready.

steps.title: Add RT mastermix
steps.instruction: Add 98.5 µl of the prepared RT mastermix to each slide.

steps.title: RT pre‑incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the slides at 65 °C for 5 min, then place them on ice for 1 min.

steps.title: Add RT enzyme
steps.instruction: Pipette 1.5 µl of Thermoscript or SuperScript III RT enzyme onto all slides except the no‑RT control; mix gently by up‑and‑down pipetting.

steps.title: Reverse transcription cycling
steps.instruction: Run the thermal cycler: 55 °C for 30 min, 70 °C for 15 min, then hold at 4 °C (or remove and keep on ice). This is a safe pause point; keep slides covered in a fridge.

steps.title: Remove RT solution
steps.instruction: Discard the RT reaction mixture while keeping the slides on ice.

steps.title: Post‑RT water washes
steps.instruction: Wash the slides twice for 1 min each with 100 µl ice‑cold sterile water; then remove as much water as possible using a 10‑20 µl pipette.

steps.title: Prepare PCR mix
steps.instruction: Prepare a HiFi Phusion Taq PCR mix according to the kit instructions.

steps.title: PCR amplification
steps.instruction: Distribute the PCR mix equally across each slide, then run the following program: 95 °C 30 min, 95 °C 10 min, 60 °C 25 min, 72 °C 5 min; repeat the 95 °C‑10 min, 60 °C‑25 min, 72 °C‑5 min cycle 20–35 times; then 72 °C 7 min, hold at 10 °C. Remove the frame‑seal chamber before the final incubation and place the slide in a small plastic box to minimise evaporation.

steps.title: Post‑PCR cleanup
steps.instruction: Pipette off the remaining PCR solution, then wash the slides twice for 5 min each with 100 µl 1× PBS.

steps.title: Block slides
steps.instruction: Add 100 µl of 1× Block solution (10 mg BSA dissolved in 1 ml 10× PBS) to each slide and incubate on ice for 30 min.

steps.title: Prepare antibody dilution
steps.instruction: Dilute anti‑DIG‑AP antibody 1:500 in 1× Block solution and keep on ice.

steps.title: Remove excess block
steps.instruction: Aspirate as much of the 1× Block solution as possible from each slide.

steps.title: Apply primary antibody
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl of the diluted anti‑DIG‑AP antibody to each slide and incubate at room temperature for 1 hour.

steps.title: Wash after antibody
steps.instruction: Remove the antibody solution and wash the slides twice for 15 min each at room temperature in Wash Buffer 2 (0.1 M Tris‑HCl, 0.15 M NaCl, pH 9.5). Peels may be transferred to a new microscope slide if desired; keep them immersed in Wash Buffer 2.

steps.title: Final wash before staining
steps.instruction: Discard Wash Buffer 2.

steps.title: AP substrate staining
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl of BM Purple (AP substrate) to each slide, incubate in the dark on ice. Stain for 10 min to 2 h; if no signal after 1 h, add another 50 µl of BM Purple and continue incubation.

steps.title: Remove excess stain
steps.instruction: Add 100 µl Wash Buffer 2 and wash the slides three times for 5 min each to eliminate residual stain and debris.

steps.title: Final water rinse
steps.instruction: Wash the slides once with sterile water, then remove all water.

steps.title: Mount in glycerol
steps.instruction: Mount the peels with 40 µl of 40 % glycerol (use 40–150 µl depending on the number of peels); avoid excessive glycerol.

steps.title: Apply coverslip and seal
steps.instruction: Place a coverslip directly onto the glycerol‑covered peels (do not slide it), ensure it does not float (remove excess glycerol if needed), and seal the corners with nail varnish.

steps.title: Image and store slides
steps.instruction: Visualise the slides under a bright‑field microscope, using identical settings for all peels. Store the slides at room temperature; they remain usable for approximately three weeks.
